subject: Retention carveout decisions: ephemeral keys, SSO traceability & BYOK gating
summary: Triage for a ClearHealth request for short-lived key carveouts and SSO traceability requirements. Internal alignment on feasibility, gating, and next steps; schedule a focused tech/product session.
messages:
From: ClearHealth Security <security@clearhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearhealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: short-lived key carveouts + SSO token traces for pilot

Hi Lauren,

Quick note from the security team at ClearHealth — we’re starting a pilot that requires retaining limited audit traces for a 7-day window for short-lived keys used in analysis jobs. Our compliance folks want: a) proof of SSO handshakes (timestamp + subject/email) for sessions used to request ephemeral keys, and b) a narrow exception path for keys created with customer-managed KMS (BYOK) so we can meet data residency/escrow needs.

We understand you have a standard 90-day retention and BYOK model — we’re asking for a carveout for this pilot to retain only token traces (not full request bodies) for 7 days and an explicit BYOK gating checklist. Can Redwood confirm feasibility and what the product gating would look like (SLA, approvals, implementation timeline)?

I attached our requirements doc and a sample policy matrix. Would like a brief triage call this week.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Lead Security Engineer — ClearHealth
security@clearhealth.com

Attachments: clearhealth_byo_requirements_v2.pdf

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: ClearHealth Security <security@clearhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived key carveouts + SSO token traces for pilot

Ellen — thanks for the detail and the doc. Looping in Priyom (privacy/compliance engineering) and Grace (product) to triage.

High level: we can likely support a scoped 7-day audit trace for SSO handshakes and ephemeral-key issuance, but there are implementation and policy signals we need to align on:
- Exact scoped schema for the "token traces" (fields we store)
- Whether BYOK gating is a product flag (customer toggle) or an enterprise-only manual approval
- Any retention/exfiltration controls ClearHealth requires beyond the 7-day window

Propose this agenda for a 30m triage call:
1) Confirm required fields for traces
2) BYOK gating model (auto vs approval vs contract clause)
3) Risk mitigations (redaction, access control, audit log WORM)
4) Timeline and next steps (engineering estimate)

We have availability Tue/Wed afternoon PT. Would either work?

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ClearHealth Security <security@clearhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived key carveouts + SSO token traces for pilot

Quick technical note before the call:
- We differentiate between request-level logs (full request + payload) and handshake/issuance metadata. Persisting just handshake metadata (timestamp, subject, user-id/email, key-id, issuing-service, region) for 7 days is cheap and compatible with our streaming audit pipeline.
- For BYOK: if keys are customer-managed (CMK) and never leave the customer's HSM, we still record meta (key-id and KMS provider). The gating ask here is whether the customer wants Redwood to retain an escrowed wrap of the key (we do not do that today).
- Compliance controls to propose: field-level redaction, limited RBAC for trace access, short-lived pre-signed evidence bundles for audits (expires automatically).

Estimate: 2 dev-weeks to add the narrow trace schema + access controls if scoped strictly to "ephemeral issuance events" and not to broad request logging. Adding a customer toggle and admin approval flow + console UI is an additional 2–3 dev-weeks.

I’ll bring a short tech proposal to the triage call with rough API shapes and RBAC considerations.

— Priyom
Senior Software Engineer, Compliance Infrastructure

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: ClearHealth Security <security@clearhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived key carveouts + SSO token traces for pilot

Thanks all — brief product stance to help the call land:
- Priority: low-risk pilots where we do not change long-term retention defaults. This looks like a pilot with a time-boxed exception (7 days) and strict scope.
- Approval model: recommend a product-flag + legal/security attestation for the pilot. I prefer not to bake permanent toggles into the public console; make this an enterprise-only controlled configuration (managed by Redwood SEs + legal sign-off).
- Deliverables I want from engineering for triage: API schema for "issuance_trace", RBAC matrix for access, and an audit-ready evidence bundle design (expired links + manifest).

If ClearHealth signs for the pilot we can treat the engineering effort as a scoped spike with an acceptance checklist. I’ll prioritize backlog accordingly if legal approves.

-G
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Security

From: ClearHealth Security <security@clearhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ClearHealth Procurement <procurement@clearhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived key carveouts + SSO token traces for pilot

Lauren / Priyom / Grace — thanks for the quick responses and the proposed approach. A couple clarifications before the call:
- On schema: we only need (1) issuance_timestamp (RFC3339), (2) requesting_subject (email), (3) key_id (reference), (4) action ("issue"/"revoke"), (5) region. No request bodies, no token contents.
- BYOK: we do NOT expect Redwood to escrow our key material. We only need metadata and a signed manifest produced at issuance time that our security officer can retrieve for up to 7 days.
- Approval: procurement requires a short addendum that outlines the pilot guardrails (timebox, access controls, data types retained). Can you share a skeleton addendum?

We can do Wed 11/4 10:30am PT for the 30m triage if that works.

Thanks,
Ellen
